+//! The light-viewport inks (#698): on a light ground the viewport's
+//! overlay, wire and palette inks flip to darker sets that clear 3:1
+//! (WCAG 1.4.11) against the ground, while the dark set stays the house
+//! look byte for byte. The dark values are the consts they already were
+//! (interact.rs, boundary_viz.rs, colorvision's EDGE_WIRE); the light
+//! values are ours, pinned by `viewport_ground_tests`.
+//! Provenance: our own palette, specced from the WCAG 2.x contrast
+//! definition `contrast` implements; no HSMWorks material consulted.
+
+use egui::Color32;
+
+use super::colorvision::{EDGE_WIRE, Semantic};
+use super::{contrast, theme};
+
+/// The luminance past which a ground counts as light (mid-grey sits at
+/// 0.18; dark's ink is 0.02, light's 0.85).
+const LIGHT_GROUND: f64 = 0.18;
+
+/// Whether a ground reads light.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn light_ground(ground: Color32) -> bool {
+    contrast::luma(ground) > LIGHT_GROUND
+}
+
+/// The wireframe line on a light viewport: the dark ground's cool gray
+/// vanishes on paper, so the light ground gets a dark ink (8:1 on the
+/// light viewport, pinned).
+const EDGE_WIRE_LIGHT: [f32; 3] = [0.20, 0.23, 0.28];
+
+/// The wireframe edge ink for a ground (viewport `fs_edge`'s `gray`).
+#[must_use]
+pub const fn wire_ink(light: bool) -> [f32; 3] {
+    if light { EDGE_WIRE_LIGHT } else { EDGE_WIRE }
+}
+
+impl Semantic {
+    /// The house palette on a light viewport: the move kinds and the
+    /// boundary roles as tuned on screen (#698). Verdict and selection
+    /// inks are unchanged: they paint the stock and the selected part,
+    /// not lines on the ground.
+    pub const OFF_LIGHT_GROUND: Semantic = Semantic {
+        feed: [0.08, 0.36, 0.12],
+        rapid: [0.01, 0.31, 0.90],
+        plunge: [0.90, 0.13, 0.13],
+        bound_include: [0.10, 0.80, 1.00],
+        bound_exclude: [1.00, 0.20, 0.70],
+        bound_open: [1.00, 0.65, 0.05],
+        ..Semantic::OFF
+    };
+
+    /// Protan/deutan on a light viewport: the same blue-yellow axis as
+    /// `RED_GREEN`, darkened to clear 3:1 - gold feed and exclude against
+    /// the blue rapid and include; plunge and open go near-black, the
+    /// lightness end the dark ground's white open and pale inks held.
+    pub const RED_GREEN_LIGHT_GROUND: Semantic = Semantic {
+        feed: [0.55, 0.42, 0.00],
+        rapid: [0.01, 0.31, 0.90],
+        plunge: [0.22, 0.08, 0.00],
+        bound_include: [0.00, 0.30, 0.85],
+        bound_exclude: [0.55, 0.42, 0.00],
+        bound_open: [0.12, 0.12, 0.12],
+        ..Semantic::RED_GREEN
+    };
+
+    /// Tritan on a light viewport: red-cyan survives - the deep green
+    /// feed, red plunge and exclude, a teal include; rapid and open go
+    /// near-black so lightness parts them from the green.
+    pub const TRITAN_LIGHT_GROUND: Semantic = Semantic {
+        feed: [0.08, 0.36, 0.12],
+        rapid: [0.05, 0.05, 0.12],
+        plunge: [0.90, 0.13, 0.13],
+        bound_include: [0.00, 0.40, 0.45],
+        bound_exclude: [0.80, 0.05, 0.10],
+        bound_open: [0.12, 0.12, 0.12],
+        ..Semantic::TRITAN
+    };
+}
+
+/// The viewport overlay inks that were tuned against the dark ground.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum Overlay {
+    Region,
+    Retract,
+    Cut,
+    Pick,
+    Hover,
+}
+
+/// An overlay ink on a ground: the dark consts as they were, or the
+/// light set (each clears 3:1 on the light viewport; the test pins it).
+#[must_use]
+pub fn overlay_ink(o: Overlay, light: bool) -> [f32; 3] {
+    match (o, light) {
+        (Overlay::Region, false) => crate::interact::REGION_RGB,
+        (Overlay::Region, true) => [0.70, 0.35, 0.00],
+        (Overlay::Retract, false) => crate::interact::RETRACT_RGB,
+        (Overlay::Retract, true) => [0.05, 0.40, 0.75],
+        (Overlay::Cut, false) => crate::interact::CUT_RGB,
+        (Overlay::Cut, true) => [0.70, 0.12, 0.10],
+        (Overlay::Pick, false) => crate::interact::PICK_RGB,
+        (Overlay::Pick, true) => [0.45, 0.15, 0.62],
+        (Overlay::Hover, false) => crate::boundary_viz::HOVER_RGB,
+        (Overlay::Hover, true) => [0.70, 0.40, 0.00],
+    }
+}
+
+/// The overlay ink for the live theme's viewport ground.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn overlay(o: Overlay) -> [f32; 3] {
+    overlay_ink(o, light_ground(theme::current().viewport))
+}
+
+/// The viewport furniture's greys: the view cube, its nav buttons, the
+/// corner hint and the playback tool marker. On the dark ground they
+/// are the values the cube always drew; on a light ground the faces are
+/// a grey a step darker than the viewport, the edges darker still, and
+/// the labels and button glyphs dark ink.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct CubeInk {
+    /// Face grey at the darkest head-light angle, and its span.
+    pub face_base: f32,
+    pub face_span: f32,
+    /// Added to a hovered face (or button) grey.
+    pub hover_lift: u8,
+    /// Face and button outline.
+    pub edge: Color32,
+    /// Face label.
+    pub label: Color32,
+    /// Button fill, and whether the button wears the edge outline.
+    pub button: u8,
+    pub outline_buttons: bool,
+    /// Button glyph when its toggle is on, and when off.
+    pub glyph_on: Color32,
+    pub glyph_off: Color32,
+    /// The viewport's corner control hint.
+    pub hint: Color32,
+    /// The tool-position marker (stem, ring, centre dot) of playback.
+    pub marker: [Color32; 3],
+    /// The Axes button's X, Y, Z triad.
+    pub triad: [Color32; 3],
+}
+
+/// The cube greys for a ground.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn cube_ink(light: bool) -> CubeInk {
+    if light {
+        CubeInk {
+            face_base: 165.0,
+            face_span: 40.0,
+            hover_lift: 30,
+            edge: Color32::from_gray(90),
+            label: Color32::from_gray(20),
+            button: 185,
+            outline_buttons: true,
+            glyph_on: Color32::from_gray(10),
+            glyph_off: Color32::from_gray(60),
+            hint: Color32::from_gray(60),
+            marker: [Color32::from_gray(50), Color32::from_gray(40), Color32::from_gray(20)],
+            triad: [Color32::from_rgb(215, 20, 20), Color32::from_rgb(0, 140, 30), Color32::from_rgb(20, 70, 230)],
+        }
+    } else {
+        CubeInk {
+            face_base: 46.0,
+            face_span: 46.0,
+            hover_lift: 52,
+            edge: Color32::from_white_alpha(170),
+            label: Color32::from_white_alpha(230),
+            button: 46,
+            outline_buttons: false,
+            glyph_on: Color32::WHITE,
+            glyph_off: Color32::from_white_alpha(160),
+            hint: Color32::from_white_alpha(200),
+            marker: [Color32::from_gray(225), Color32::from_gray(240), Color32::WHITE],
+            triad: [Color32::from_rgb(245, 70, 70), Color32::from_rgb(60, 220, 80), Color32::from_rgb(90, 140, 255)],
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// The cube greys for the live theme's viewport ground.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn cube() -> CubeInk {
+    cube_ink(light_ground(theme::current().viewport))
+}
+
+/// How much of its own colour an unselected path keeps on a light
+/// ground: it fades toward the ground (a dimmed line on paper is a
+/// paler one), never toward black, which turns every hue to ink.
+const LIGHT_DIM_KEEP: f32 = 0.6;
+
+/// A path colour dimmed by `dim` (1.0 = selected, untouched). The dark
+/// ground scales toward black as it always did; a light ground fades
+/// toward the ground itself, keeping the hue readable.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn dimmed(base: [f32; 3], dim: f32, ground: Color32) -> [f32; 3] {
+    if dim >= 1.0 {
+        return base;
+    }
+    if !light_ground(ground) {
+        return [base[0] * dim, base[1] * dim, base[2] * dim];
+    }
+    let g = [ground.r(), ground.g(), ground.b()].map(|c| f32::from(c) / 255.0);
+    let k = LIGHT_DIM_KEEP;
+    [0, 1, 2].map(|i| base[i] * k + g[i] * (1.0 - k))
+}

+## #698 - Light theme gets a light viewport
+
+**What was decided.** The viewport ground is a theme token (`Tokens::viewport`:
+the dark column keeps today's clear colour, the light column is `#DDE1E7`).
+Theme files can set it as `viewport`. The 3D pass clears to the live theme's
+ground. Everything drawn over the viewport that assumed a dark ground now has
+a light-ground value. The dark column is unchanged in value; each dark ink is
+asserted equal to its old constant.
+
+The light values were tuned on screen with the reporter, in a running build:
+
+- **Toolpath moves** (`Semantic::OFF_LIGHT_GROUND`): feed is a deep green
+  `[0.08, 0.36, 0.12]`. Rapid `[0.01, 0.31, 0.90]` and plunge
+  `[0.90, 0.13, 0.13]` were measured off strokes the reporter drew on a
+  screenshot. All three clear 3:1 on the ground.
+- **Boundary roles**: saturated include/exclude/open
+  (`[0.10, 0.80, 1.00]`, `[1.00, 0.20, 0.70]`, `[1.00, 0.65, 0.05]`).
+  These do not clear 3:1, a trade for hue (see Open).
+- **Colour-vision modes** (review of PR #838): protan/deutan and tritan get
+  light-ground sets too (`RED_GREEN_LIGHT_GROUND`, `TRITAN_LIGHT_GROUND`),
+  changing only the line inks. Their dark-tuned lines read 1.01-2.8:1 on the
+  light ground (pale yellow feed, white "open" boundary). Each light set keeps
+  its eye's surviving axis (blue-yellow; red-cyan) and moves the pale end to
+  near-black, so lightness still carries the pairs. Every must-distinguish
+  pair passes the M13.4 CIEDE2000 floor (weakest: protan 25.7, deutan 27.7,
+  tritan 24.4), and every line ink clears 3:1 (3.5-14.6:1). The values were
+  found with a port of `cvd.rs`'s maths and are pinned by
+  `the_light_colour_vision_sets_pass_the_cvd_gate_and_clear_3_to_1`. Stock
+  verdict and selection inks are unchanged: they paint the part, not lines on
+  the ground.
+- **Dimmed paths** (unselected, under "Show all toolpaths"): on a light ground
+  they fade toward the ground, keeping 60% of their colour
+  (`ground_ink::dimmed`). Scaling toward black (the dark ground's rule,
+  `OTHERS_DIM` 0.45) turned every hue into near-black ink on a light ground.
+  This was the real reason the first colour rounds all "looked the same".
+- **View cube and its four buttons** (`ground_ink::cube_ink`): faces are mid
+  grey 165-205, a step under the ground. Edges and button outlines are grey
+  90. Labels and glyphs are near-black. The Axes button's triad is an
+  isometric triad (equal arms, 120 degrees apart), centred, in saturated
+  X/Y/Z colours (it was off-centre and pastel in both themes).
+- **Corner control hint and playback tool marker**: dark grey on a light
+  ground. Both were fixed white.
+- **Hover** (light only): `field_hover` equals the viewport grey `#DDE1E7`,
+  and egui's own hover uses it too, with dark ink. The dark-column hover
+  (steel-blue accent, white ink) is unchanged.
+- **Window title bars** (light only): `widgets.open.weak_bg_fill` is the
+  window fill and `open.fg_stroke` the text. They were egui's dark defaults
+  in every theme, so a light window had a black title bar. Dark keeps egui's
+  own values, pinned by `the_dark_title_bar_keeps_eguis_own_open_fill`.
+- **Debug info window** draws its own title row (`window_chrome`): the
+  collapse arrow hovers grey and close hovers red with a white cross, like
+  the OS window's caption buttons. egui's built-in title bar paints these
+  glyphs with no hover fill and cannot be styled to do so. It is in this PR
+  because the reporter hit it during the light-theme check: on the light
+  ground the window's arrow and close glyphs were invisible, then vanished
+  on hover. It is a light-theme readability fix, not a new feature.
+
+**Why.** The reporter asked for a light viewport in the light theme. A first
+pass derived from the WCAG 3:1 floor read muddy on 1 px lines. The reporter's
+on-screen picks are what ships, with the 3:1 floor kept where it held (moves,
+overlays, wire, axes, cube ink, hint, marker, hover ink).
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+- Keep the viewport dark in every theme: rejected, it is the bug as reported.
+- Thicker toolpath lines on a light ground: not needed once the dim rule was
+  fixed. A 1 px line carries the reporter's colours exactly.
+- A darker light ground (`#C4C8CE`): tried and reverted at the reporter's call.
+- A pale-blue light hover (`selection_bg`), then the cube's grey 185 and 205:
+  tried in turn, and the viewport grey was chosen.
+- Re-styling egui's built-in window title bar: not possible in egui 0.36
+  (the caption glyphs have no hover fill), hence our own title row.
+
+**Open (for the maintainer).**
+1. Boundary role inks on the light ground are under 3:1 (hue over contrast).
+   They are pinned as chosen by `the_light_palette_is_the_hand_tuned_set`.
+2. The light colour-vision sets were checked by the simulation gate, not by a
+   colour-vision-deficient viewer.
+3. Part shading and the selected-part amber on the light ground were not
+   re-tuned.
+4. The other four floating windows still use egui's title bar (now themed,
+   but with no caption hover fill). They can adopt `window_chrome::title_row`.
+5. The light pixel snapshot golden (`egui_app_light`) will differ. It is
+   regenerated only at a cut (pixel-snapshot law); this PR touches no PNG.
+6. `theme.rs` is at 402 lines.
+7. The light-set literals live in `ground_ink.rs`, not in theme tokens, so a
+   theme file cannot change them yet (review note 4: a follow-up).
+
+**Cost to change later.** Each light ink is one value in `ground_ink.rs` or
+the light `Tokens` column, and its test.
